scope.evidence_basis: Actual original-source comparison and local derivation reread: Recomputed K1=C1 C0 T^(-1/p)G+T^(1-1/q)D. The weak-space W11 bound supplies continuous A1 representatives while cone membership is only a.e. Markov on the L1 gauge gives |E_R|<=T^(1-1/p)G/R. The amplitude gives an L1(A1) tail <=K1|E_R|. Compact gauge balls and the finite-net hull lemma supply compact interval integrals without adding cone points. For q=1, finite-p translations use the bounded-amplitude estimate; for q>1, supremum translations use Holder. Two-point Ehrling, eta before indices, gives a Cauchy subsequence in Lp(A0). The p=infinity representative extension uses a full-measure dense set and no cone closedness. This proof avoids the time-dependent selection following source (2.8). The source concern is not a disproof of Theorem 1 and is nonessential to the reconstructed proof.

N-cone-mechanism: Derive the A1 supremum bound and control the gauge-truncation tail.
Obtain compact interval integrals and apply Simon using the correct derivative exponent.
Upgrade weak-space Cauchy convergence with the two-point Ehrling estimate.
